finding.claim: webhookUrl path is NOT a finding: regex is a full-string match fixing host to hooks.example.com with alnum-only path, so no host or userinfo bypass
finding.guards_checked: Full-string regex match; fixed host; alnum-only path excludes @, ?, #, other hosts

verdict.guard_found: src/Profile.java:12: `webhook.matches("https://hooks\\.example\\.com/[A-Za-z0-9]{20}")` is a full-string anchored match (String.matches requires the whole input to match). It fixes the scheme and host to hooks.example.com and allows only 20 alphanumeric characters in the path, so there is no room for userinfo (@), query, fragment, or a different host. Line 13 throws on mismatch, so nothing unvalidated is stored at line 15.
verdict.reason: The webhook value is attacker-settable through update() (src/Profile.java:11), but the anchored full-match at src/Profile.java:12 fixes the host to hooks.example.com with an alphanumeric-only path, so the URI passed to URI.create at src/Profile.java:21 cannot point anywhere else; the trace lines are accurate. Out of scope for this candidate: iconUrl is stored unvalidated at src/Profile.java:16 and fetched with GET at src/Profile.java:23-24, which may be a separate SSRF worth its own review.
